breakfast.name: Gromperekichelcher (Potato Fritters)
instructions: Grate potatoes, squeeze dry
Mix with onion, eggs, flour, parsley
Fry spoonfuls until crispy and golden
breakfast.description: Crispy potato fritters — Luxembourg's signature comfort food.

breakfast.name: Luxembourgish Croissant with Jam
instructions: Warm croissant
Spread with butter and plum jam
breakfast.description: Buttery croissant with Luxembourg plum preserve.

breakfast.name: Mettwurscht (Raw Pork Spread)
instructions: Mettwurscht is Luxembourg's spreadable raw pork sausage — cured with salt and spice
Spread generously on dark bread
Top with raw onion rings
Crack black pepper over generously
Serve with pickles alongside
Mettwurscht is a German-Luxembourgish tradition — a breakfast charcuterie
The raw pork is safe due to the salt curing and the tradition of quality
Only eat from trusted sources — quality is essential
The combination of raw meat spread, raw onion, and dark bread is simple and bold
Luxembourg's German culinary heritage is strongest in the charcuterie tradition
breakfast.description: Luxembourg's raw pork spread — cured pork sausage spread thickly on dark bread with raw onion rings and cracked pepper. The German-Luxembourgish charcuterie tradition at its most direct. The salt curing makes it safe; the raw pork-onion-bread combination is bold and simple. A breakfast for people who mean business.

breakfast.name: Luxemburger Millerahmstrudel (Cream Strudel)
ingredients: Strudel dough (flour, oil, warm water, vinegar)
instructions: Pull strudel dough until it's thin as a tablecloth — the stretching technique takes practice
The dough should be translucent when held to light
Spread cream cheese filling mixed with sour cream, egg, sugar, vanilla
Scatter raisins
Roll using the tablecloth — rolling without tearing is the skill
Brush with melted butter generously
Bake until golden and the pastry is shatteringly thin
The cream filling should be just set
Millerahmstrudel is Luxembourg's cream strudel — French and German pastry traditions combined
The paper-thin pulled dough is the technique that separates strudel from other pastries
breakfast.description: Luxembourg's cream strudel — pulled paper-thin strudel dough filled with cream cheese, sour cream, and vanilla, baked until the thin pastry shatters. The strudel-pulling technique (until the dough is tablecloth-thin) combines German and French pastry traditions — exactly Luxembourg's culinary identity.

lunch.name: Judd mat Gaardebounen (Smoked Pork with Beans)
instructions: Soak pork overnight
Simmer pork 90 min until tender
Cook broad beans and potatoes
Make cream sauce with cooking liquid
Slice pork, serve with beans, potatoes, and cream sauce
lunch.description: Luxembourg's national dish — smoked pork neck with broad beans.

lunch.name: Bouneschlupp (Green Bean Soup)
instructions: Sauté bacon and onion
Add beans, potatoes, water
Simmer 25 min
Add cream and savory
Blend partially for texture
lunch.description: Creamy green bean soup with bacon.

lunch.name: Träipen (Black Pudding)
ingredients: Träipen (Luxembourg-style black pudding with cabbage and oats)
instructions: Pan-fry träipen slices in butter until the outside is crispy
The inside should remain soft and dense
Serve with boiled potatoes and apple sauce
Träipen is Luxembourg's black pudding — but it includes cabbage and oats in the mix
The vegetable inclusion makes it less heavy than pure blood sausage
The crispy exterior and the soft, savory interior are the textural contrast
Träipen is Luxembourg's most distinctive charcuterie
The combination of pig blood, oats, and cooked cabbage is unique
Apple sauce provides sweetness and acidity against the rich blood sausage
Luxembourg's märt (traditional autumn pig festival) is when träipen is made
lunch.description: Luxembourg's distinctive black pudding — blood sausage made with cooked cabbage and oats incorporated into the mix, making it lighter than pure blood sausage, fried crispy and served with apple sauce. The vegetable-oat inclusion is uniquely Luxembourgish. Made at the autumn märt festival when pigs are processed.

lunch.name: Feierstengszalot (Potato Salad)
instructions: Boil waxy potatoes until just tender — peel while still warm
Slice thickly while warm — the warmth helps the dressing absorb
Make a warm vinaigrette: warm beef stock, white wine vinegar, oil, mustard, onion
Pour over the warm potatoes — the stock is absorbed
Season generously — potato salad needs more salt than you expect
Add herbs while still warm
This is a German-style potato salad (vinaigrette, not mayo)
Feierstengszalot is the traditional Luxembourg potato salad — served with Fiersteng steak
The warm beef stock dressing is the technique that makes it absorb so well
Luxembourg's French wine and German potato culture combined in this salad
lunch.description: Luxembourg's traditional potato salad — waxy potato slices dressed while warm with beef stock, white wine vinegar, mustard, and onion. The warm stock dressing is the German technique: it absorbs into the potato instead of coating it, creating a richer, more integrated flavor than mayonnaise-based versions.

lunch.name: Rieslingspaschtéit (Riesling Pie)
instructions: Make pastry crust — shortcrust or puff
Fill with seasoned pork-veal mixture
Add shallots, herbs, seasoning
Pour in Riesling and cream — the wine goes in raw with the filling
Seal with pastry lid — decorative crimping
Bake at 180°C for 50-60 minutes
The Riesling and cream bake into a sauce inside the sealed pastry
Slice to reveal the steaming, wine-fragrant interior
Rieslingspaschtéit is Luxembourg's most celebrated dish
The Moselle Riesling from Luxembourg's wine region is the specific grape
lunch.description: Luxembourg's signature pie — pork and veal sealed in pastry with Moselle Riesling and cream, baked until the wine reduces inside the sealed crust into a fragrant sauce. Rieslingspaschtéit is Luxembourg's national dish. The Moselle Riesling — from Luxembourg's own wine region — is the specific and irreplaceable ingredient.

dinner.name: Riesling Haam (Riesling Ham)
instructions: Place ham in pot with wine, vegetables, herbs
Simmer 90 min
Remove ham, reduce sauce with cream
Slice ham, pour sauce over
Serve with boiled potatoes
dinner.description: Ham braised in Luxembourg Riesling wine.

dinner.name: Kniddelen (Dumplings)
instructions: Mix batter until smooth
Drop spoonfuls into boiling water
Cook until they float
Toss with bacon and cream sauce
dinner.description: Simple flour dumplings in bacon cream sauce.

dinner.name: Kachkéis (Cancoillotte-Style Melted Cheese)
ingredients: Kachkéis (Luxembourg cooked cheese — sour milk processed)
instructions: Melt kachkéis in a small pot over low heat with butter
Stir until smooth — it becomes a pourable, fondue-like cheese sauce
Season with caraway seeds
Pour over boiled potatoes or serve with bread for dipping
Kachkéis is Luxembourg's most beloved processed cheese
It's made from sour milk — fermented first, then cooked
The flavor is pungent, tangy, deeply savory
Kachkéis is Luxembourg's fondue — the communal melted cheese
Found in every Luxembourg supermarket, made by many local producers
The caraway-and-cheese combination is specifically Luxembourgish
dinner.description: Luxembourg's melted national cheese — kachkéis (cooked sour milk cheese) melted with butter into a pourable, pungent, fondue-like sauce over potatoes or bread. The fermented sour milk base gives it a sharper, more pungent flavor than Swiss fondue. Kachkéis is Luxembourg's most beloved domestic food product.

dinner.name: Gehäkkeltes (Minced Meat Stew)
ingredients: Potatoes or egg noodles for serving
instructions: Brown minced meat in a pot — break up lumps
Add onion, carrot, celery — saute
Add tomato paste, cook briefly — frying the paste reduces the raw flavor
Add white wine, reduce
Add stock, thyme, bay leaf
Simmer 30-40 minutes
The result is a hearty, simple minced meat stew
Serve over boiled potatoes or egg noodles
Gehäkkeltes is Luxembourg's weeknight dinner — unfussy, filling, reliable
The white wine enriches without overwhelming — Luxembourg's cooking is wine-forward
dinner.description: Luxembourg's weeknight stew — minced pork braised with vegetables, white wine, and stock into a hearty, unfussy dinner. White wine appears naturally in Luxembourg's cooking because the country produces its own Moselle wines. Served over potatoes or egg noodles, this is Luxembourg's most democratic daily dinner.

dinner.name: Äppelklatzen (Stuffed Baked Apple)
instructions: Core the apples — remove the core but leave the base intact
Mix marzipan with cinnamon, raisins, walnuts
Stuff the cavity with marzipan mixture
Place in a baking dish
Top each apple with a knob of butter
Bake at 180°C until the apple is very soft and the top is slightly caramelized
The marzipan melts into the apple cavity
Serve with vanilla sauce
Äppelklatzen is Luxembourg's traditional dessert — baked apple elevated by marzipan
The almond-apple flavor combination is the Luxembourg dessert signature
dinner.description: Luxembourg's baked apple — cored apples stuffed with marzipan, cinnamon, and walnuts, roasted until the apple softens and the marzipan melts into the cavity. The almond-apple pairing is Luxembourg's dessert signature, reflecting the country's orchard culture and its German-French almond pastry influence.

snacks.name: Verwurrelter (Fried Pastry Twists)
instructions: Mix dough with kirsch
Roll thin, cut strips
Twist into knots
Deep fry until golden
Dust with powdered sugar
snacks.description: Knotted fried pastries dusted with sugar — carnival treat.

snacks.name: Pâté de Campagne (Country Terrine)
ingredients: Pork liver, pork belly, pork shoulder
instructions: Grind or process pork shoulder and belly coarsely
Blend liver more finely
Mix all meats with onion, garlic, thyme, quatre épices, eggs, cream, armagnac
Season generously — cold fat dulls salt, so season boldly
Line a terrine mold with larding fat or bacon
Fill with the meat mixture, pack firmly
Cover with more bacon, add a bay leaf on top
Bake in a bain-marie 90 minutes — slow, gentle cooking
Refrigerate 24-48 hours before serving — it improves enormously
Pâté de campagne represents Luxembourg's French culinary identity — charcuterie tradition
snacks.description: Luxembourg's French charcuterie — pork and liver terrine spiced with quatre épices and armagnac, baked in a water bath and rested for two days. The 48-hour rest before slicing is mandatory: the flavors integrate and the texture firms. Luxembourg's French culinary identity at its most pronounced.

snacks.name: Crêpes Dentelles (Lace Pancakes)
instructions: Make a very thin, loose batter — thinner than regular crepes
Rest 30 minutes
Use a wide, hot pan — very thin film of butter
Pour the minimum possible batter — tilt to create the thinnest possible crepe
The edges should be lacy and brown — like old lace
Cook until the surface is completely dry and the lace edges are crispy
The center should be almost paper-thin
Roll or fold — the crepe should be crispy
Luxembourg's French culinary influence: crepes made ultra-thin, almost lace
Served with sugar and lemon or jam — the French way
snacks.description: Luxembourg's French-influenced lace pancakes — crepe batter poured so thin that the edges become genuinely lacy and the center paper-thin. The French crepe technique elevated to its extreme: less batter, hotter pan, more patience. The crispier result (more lace, less dough) is the Luxembourg interpretation.

snacks.name: Kassbréider (Cheese Wafers)
instructions: Mix finely grated cheese with a touch of flour and egg white — just enough to bind
Add caraway seeds or pepper
Drop small spoonfuls on a lined baking sheet
Flatten slightly
Bake at 200°C until melted, spread, and golden — about 8-10 minutes
They spread into thin, crispy, lacy cheese wafers
Cool on the sheet — they crisp further as they cool
The cheese wafer is Luxembourg's cocktail hour snack
The Luxembourg tradition of Aperitif culture (influenced by France) produces these
Simple, elegant, and intensely cheesy — the aperitif snack of small countries with good cheese
snacks.description: Luxembourg's aperitif wafer — grated Gruyère bound with egg white, spread thin and baked until lacy and golden. The French aperitif culture that Luxembourg absorbed produces these intensely cheesy, paper-thin wafers. Caraway seeds or black pepper are the only additions needed. Served with Moselle Riesling before dinner.

desserts.name: Quetschentaart (Plum Tart)
ingredients: Tart dough: flour, butter, sugar, egg
instructions: Make tart dough, line pan
Arrange plums cut-side up
Sprinkle sugar and cinnamon
Bake at 180°C 40 min
Serve with whipped cream
desserts.description: Open-faced plum tart — Luxembourg autumn tradition.

desserts.name: Friedkuche (Fried Pastry)
instructions: Make a soft yeast or baking powder dough
Rest 30 minutes
Roll out and cut into shapes
Deep fry at 170°C until golden
Roll in powdered sugar immediately
Optional: make a slit and pipe jam inside
Friedkuche are Luxembourg's carnival pastries — similar to doughnuts
Made for Féierwon (carnival) in February
The powdered sugar cloud and the fried dough are the carnival joy
Luxembourgers consume an outsized quantity of fried pastry at Féierwon
desserts.description: Luxembourg's carnival pastry — simple fried dough rolled in powdered sugar, made for Féierwon (carnival) in February. The powdered sugar cloud, the warm fried dough, and the carnival context are the whole experience. Luxembourg's Féierwon produces an outsized consumption of fried pastries.

desserts.name: Mirabellenkuchen (Mirabelle Plum Cake)
ingredients: Mirabelle plums (the small golden plums of the Luxembourg Moselle valley)
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs
Fold in flour and baking powder
Pour into a round baking tin
Halve and pit mirabelle plums — place cut side down over the batter
Dust with cinnamon sugar
Bake at 175°C until the batter is cooked through and the plums are soft
Glaze with warm apricot jam
Mirabelle plums are Luxembourg's most cherished fruit — grown in the Moselle valley
The small, sweet-tart golden plums appear for a few weeks in August
Mirabellenkuchen is the August ritual — everyone bakes one when the plums arrive
The golden plum halves in a pattern on the cake are the quintessential Luxembourg image
desserts.description: Luxembourg's August ritual cake — mirabelle plum halves (the small golden plums from the Moselle valley, ripe for only a few weeks) arranged over a butter cake and baked until soft. The mirabelle is Luxembourg's most cherished fruit. When they arrive in August, everyone bakes this cake. The brief season makes it more precious.

desserts.name: Floating Islands with Riesling (Îles Flottantes)
instructions: Make crème anglaise: heat milk, vanilla, Riesling
Whisk egg yolks and sugar, add to warm milk
Cook gently until it coats a spoon — the custard shouldn't scramble
The Riesling adds acidity and mineral freshness to the custard
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks with sugar
Poach large quenelles of meringue in hot milk — 2 minutes each side
Float meringue islands on the custard lake
Îles flottantes with Riesling is Luxembourg's French dessert with a local twist
The Moselle Riesling in the custard is the Luxembourg signature
Light, elegant, and wine-forward — French technique, Luxembourg ingredient
desserts.description: Luxembourg's wine-infused French dessert — soft poached meringue islands floating on crème anglaise made with Moselle Riesling. The Riesling adds mineral acidity to the custard that no other ingredient can. French technique completely — but the Luxembourg wine makes it their own.

drinks.name: Moselle Riesling
instructions: Serve chilled
Pair with Judd mat Gaardebounen or river fish
drinks.description: Crisp Riesling from Luxembourg's Moselle Valley.

drinks.name: Kachkéis Cocktail (Kirsch Coffee)
instructions: Brew strong coffee
Add kirsch and sugar
Float cream on top
drinks.description: Coffee spiked with cherry brandy and cream.

drinks.name: Crémant de Luxembourg (Sparkling Wine)
ingredients: Crémant de Luxembourg (traditional method sparkling wine from Moselle)
Optional: cassis or elderflower for a Kir variation
instructions: Chill the Crémant de Luxembourg — serve at 6-8°C
Pour into flutes — fill 3/4 full
The bubbles should be fine and persistent
Crémant de Luxembourg uses traditional method (like Champagne) but different grapes
Elbling is the unique ancient grape variety used
Riesling, Pinot blanc, Auxerrois also used
The wine is lighter and drier than Champagne — more mineral
For Kir: add a small amount of cassis at the bottom before pouring
Luxembourg wine tourism is small but the quality is genuine
Crémant de Luxembourg is the country's proudest liquid export
drinks.description: Luxembourg's sparkling pride — traditional method sparkling wine from the Moselle valley, made with the ancient Elbling grape and others. Lighter and more mineral than Champagne. Luxembourg's 1,300-hectare wine region produces outstanding Crémant that rarely leaves the country — a best-kept secret of European wine.

drinks.name: Träipenzeréng (Pig Festival Brandy)
ingredients: Mirabelle eau-de-vie or Quetsch plum brandy
Optional: served warm as a digestif
instructions: Luxembourg produces fruit brandies from Moselle valley plums
Mirabelle eau-de-vie: distilled from the small golden plums
Quetsch: distilled from purple plums
Serve neat in a small glass — room temperature or slightly cool
Sip slowly — fruit brandies should be savored
The spirit should be clear, with the pure fruit aroma
The fruit flavor is the entire experience — no additions
Luxembourg fruit brandies are artisanal — family distillers still operate
The plum brandy tradition is ancient in the Moselle region
Served at the märt (autumn pig festival) as a celebration spirit
drinks.description: Luxembourg's fruit brandy tradition — mirabelle or quetsch plum eau-de-vie distilled from the Moselle valley's stone fruits. Artisanal family distillers still operate. Clear, pure, intensely fruity — served neat as a digestif or at the autumn pig festival (märt). The plum brandy tradition is the Moselle valley's liquid heritage.
